newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli ministries to decide where to cut budgets.
newsitem.headline: Israeli ministries to decide where to cut budgets.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has agreed in principle to a Treasury plan allowing individual ministries to decide where to make further spending cuts in their 1997 budgets, Treasury sources said on Sunday.

The plan covers the approximately two billion shekels ($615 million) in additional budget cuts the Treasury is preparing for the 1997 year. These are coming on top of the 4.9 billion shekel reduction originally proposed.

Under the plan, each ministry will be given a global figure for additional spending cuts but will be free to decide where to make them. Treasury sources said there would be some guidelines, including bans against cuts in capital spending and in transfer payments to the disadvantaged.
If approved by the cabinet, it will mark the first time the Treasury's budget division has surrendered control over budget line items.

The Treasury is expected to ask the cabinet to authorise cuts of 1.5-2.3 billion shekels. The final figure will depend on the government's November tax revenues, which are due to be released later on Sunday.

The Treasury faces an uphill battle to win the second round of spending cuts. The original 4.9 billion shekel reduction, which is now with parliament, has met strong opposition even among coalition legislators.
The cabinet is expected to vote on the second-round cuts next Monday. The budget must be approved by December 31.
